The study was conducted in a globally distributed systems development (ISD) team.
The team consisted of 10 members from different countries.
The study used a qualitative research design.
The data was collected through interviews and observations.
The study found that team technology knowledge (TTK) is essential for effective team collaboration.
The study identified five factors that influence technology adaptation: awareness of TTK, facilitating conditions, effort expectancy, outcome expectations, and relative advantage.
The study found that effective technology adaptation leads to improved team collaboration, increased productivity, and better project outcomes.
The study identified challenges of technology adaptation in globally distributed teams, including coordination, communication, and cultural differences.
The study found that team leaders can overcome these challenges by developing and employing effective strategies for technology adaptation.

The study identified the need for future research on the impact of TTK on team performance and the development of more effective strategies for technology adaptation.
